chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man marries the woman during her waiting period and enters into her (consummates the marriage), she becomes permanently prohibited for him, whether he was knowing or ignorant; and if he does not enter into her, she becomes permissible for the ignorant one but does not become permissible for the knowing one.

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: he entered into her (consummated the marriage)
key_terms.لَمْ تَحِلَّ لَهُ: she is not permissible for him

ai.seo_question: Does a man permanently lose the right to marry a woman if he marries her during her waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permanence of the prohibition (mahramiyyah) in cases of marriage during 'iddah, a scenario often discussed alongside khula' or faskh. It establishes that consummation (dukhul) creates an irrevocable bond for both the knowledgeable and ignorant parties, whereas non-consummation allows the ignorant man to remarry her, highlighting the Shia juristic emphasis on the role of knowledge in legal consequences.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man marries the woman during her waiting period and sleeps with her, she would not be Permissible for him, ever, whether he was knowing or ignorant; and if he does no copulate with her, she would be Permissible for the ignorant but would not be Permissible for the other (the knowing one)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If one marries a woman during her waiting period and goes to bed with her, she becomes unlawful for him forever, regardless, he knows or not, but if he has not gone to bed with her, she is lawful for the one ignorant of her condition and is unlawful for the other (one who knows her condition).”’
